00010de0.what: Each frontier buffer holds 400 entries and nothing in the function bounds the append: counts[next] is incremented once per accepted neighbour with no compare. A wave longer than 400 entries appends from buffer 0 into buffer 1 (reproduced faithfully, which is why x and y are re-read out of the array at every use rather than latched), and a wave longer than 800 runs off the end of the array entirely, onto whatever the linker happened to put next -- which will not be what the original image had there. A tile can be queued more than once per wave, so the bound is not simply the perimeter of the range.
